ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
On a horizontal ground, there are three blocks P, Q, and R placed together, with masses $\mathbf{m}$, $2\mathrm{m}$, and $3\mathrm{m}$ respectively. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the blocks and the ground is the same. A horizontal external force of magnitude F is applied to push block P.

1. Find the ratio $\mathrm{k}$ of the magnitude of the interaction force $\mathrm{F}_{1}$ between R and Q to the magnitude of the interaction force $\mathrm{F}_{2}$ between Q and P (where $\mathbf{m}$ and F are both unknowns).

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: On a horizontal ground, three blocks P, Q, and R are placed together, with masses m, 2m, and 3m respectively. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the blocks and the ground is the same. A horizontal external force of magnitude F is applied to push block P. Find the ratio k of the magnitude of the interaction force F1 between R and Q to the magnitude of the interaction force F2 between Q and P, where m and F are both unknowns.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows three rectangular blocks touching each other on a rough horizontal surface. From left to right they are labeled P, Q, and R. A horizontal force F is applied to block P toward the right. Reasoning: Let the common kinetic friction coefficient be μ and the common acceleration of the three-block system be a to the right. The masses are m, 2m, and 3m, so the total mass is 6m. For all three blocks together, the external horizontal forces are F to the right and total kinetic friction μ(6m)g to the left, so F - μ(6m)g = 6m a. Hence a + μg = F/(6m). For block R alone, the contact force from Q on R has magnitude F1 to the right, while friction on R is μ(3m)g to the left, so F1 - μ(3m)g = 3m a. Thus F1 = 3m(a + μg) = 3m·F/(6m) = F/2. For the subsystem Q+R, the contact force from P on Q has magnitude F2 to the right, while total friction on Q+R is μ(5m)g to the left, so F2 - μ(5m)g = 5m a. Thus F2 = 5m(a + μg) = 5m·F/(6m) = 5F/6. Therefore k = F1/F2 = (F/2)/(5F/6) = 3/5.
